title: Check generated workflows against the requested job

status.capability_ready: job contract checks for chat composition (manage_workflow compose and create rerouted to compose) when the caller states a contract; without one, composition is unchanged

design.checkpoint: UI-35; no visual changes in Q-04

ownership.independent_reviewer: pending; Lapo coordinates technical review and shared-file integration

behavior: A caller can state the checkable parts of a job as a structured contract: trigger (manual; schedule with an exact cron, a cadence every hour, day, week or month, and a time zone; webhook; Jarvis event; or a piece's own trigger), sources, outputs, recipients, forbidden effects, pieces, actions, tools, channels and agents, and review items. manage_workflow compose, and create rerouted to compose, take it as an optional contract; null is none. Nothing derives a contract from free text, and the description is never rewritten.

The composer validates the contract before any provider request. A contract that cannot be read is refused as invalid. A contract no graph can keep is refused as unmeetable, judging each required step by the rules the check applies to a graph: it requires what it forbids; an output whose effects are decided when it runs while forbidding something that output could reach; an output addressed outside the recipients or to a forbidden channel; a source that does not read; a send that cannot state its recipient while recipients are limited; a cron that misses its cadence; a time zone other than the one schedules run in.

Every candidate, on the tool loop (submit_flow and inline JSON) and the one-shot path, is checked after structural validation through one acceptComposedFlow that forwards every validation argument. Departures are focused 'job contract:' errors naming the step and value, fed to the existing bounded repair loop; every repair prompt carries the contract in the job specification and every repaired candidate is checked against the same contract, so a repair cannot drop a requirement and pass.

A step reaches people when it sends or when a write addresses them (calendar attendees, a Drive share's user, a draft's receiver, a file posted to a channel); recipients are read from each step's inputs. Rejected: a different trigger kind, cron, cadence, event, piece or trigger name; a missing source or output, or the nearest step with a wrong stated value, where a source must be read by a step that reads or by the trigger; with outputs, a send or addressed write no output names, including a notification to an extra channel, in router branches and loop bodies; with recipients, reaching anyone else (cc and bcc included), a recipient decided at run time, or a send that does not state its recipient; with outputs, notification channels decided at run time; a forbidden effect, piece (the trigger included), action, tool, channel or agent; a tool chosen at run time. A destination the job does not constrain is neither checked nor claimed. Values compare the same way on both sides: a single value is a list of one, and numbers match their text.

Effects are known for the trigger (reads), notify, Jarvis reads, bounded tools (effect-capabilities.ts) and governed piece actions (piece-effects.ts). Agents, other workflows and other tools are open and can reach everything; ungoverned pieces and governed raw API calls (custom_api_call, rawGraphqlQuery, unmapped actions) are open but act only through their own service. An open step blocks when the job forbids anything it could reach; otherwise, with outputs or recipients, it is a review item and the report withholds every claim it could break. Only an output pinning an open step's action and values counts as asking for what it sends.

A passing composition returns contractReport {verified, review}, first in the manage_workflow result so its length cap cannot cut it. The journal keeps the contract as the caller gave it; manage_workflow publish and enable recheck the graph about to run against it and return contractReport with violations, also after the draft was edited, advisory like the OS warnings.
Provider failures stay failures with their errorCode, also after a contract violation; the model abstains only through report_blocked.

migration: None. The contract is an optional field of the journaled job specification (schemaVersion 1, additive); older binaries ignore it. No schema or data change.
rollback: Callers stop passing contract, and composition behaves as before. To remove the feature, revert the Q-04 commits; no data needs migrating.
limitations: The check proves stated structure, not arbitrary language: tone, content and anything only a person can judge belong in review.

Review items and the report are advisory: returned at compose, publish and enable through chat, not stored, and nothing refuses a publish or an enable on them. The dashboard's enable path does not show them yet.
Opportunity composition passes no contract yet; only chat composition can state one.
Connection credentials stay deferred to activation, which already refuses to run without them.
A bounded tool counts at its mapped category; Authority can raise a single call when it runs (write_file to a shell startup file is execute_command), and the check does not predict that raise.
Values compare exactly apart from list and number normalization, so differently cased addresses differ.
A router branch may not run; an output counts as produced when a step produces it, conditional or not.
Evaluation task specifications can carry a contract; no shipped task set does yet.
manage_workflow's emitted schema grew by about 470 B for the contract parameter; its #504 ceilings moved in their own commit with the reason.
found: Every workflow schedule runs in one process-wide time zone (lib/cron-scheduler.ts); a per-flow timezone input is ignored by the trigger manager, so a contract checks the stated zone against that one instead of the graph.

Authority classes Google Calendar create and update with attendees as write_data, although Google emails the invitations; only add and remove attendee are send_message. The contract treats any write that addresses people as reaching them.
Governed raw API actions (custom_api_call, GitHub rawGraphqlQuery) carry a worst-case category, not a bound, and ungoverned pieces run without Authority; the contract treats both as open.
next: Have opportunity composition pass a contract built from the accepted proposal's explicit fields, show the recheck on the dashboard's publish and enable path, and add contracts to evaluation task sets so hosted runs measure contract-checked composition. All are separate cards.

review.result: An independent code review found 6 blocking and 11 smaller issues and made suggestions. All are fixed in 1b64360b; each guarantee has a test that fails when it is removed (103 of 103).
blocking: S1: an open step was blocked only for forbidden effects, so an agent or another workflow passed forbidden tools, pieces, actions or agents and the report verified 'does nothing the job forbids'
S2: naming a piece as a source vouched for all its actions, so an ungoverned send by that piece passed as 'sends nothing beyond the requested outputs'
S3: sends were recognized by category only, so calendar invitations and Drive shares reached people while 'messages reach only' was verified

U1: contracts no graph can keep (a required open output against what it could reach, an output addressed outside the recipients, a required agent with agents forbidden) passed validation and used the whole repair budget
U2: a single value never matched a list of one, nor a number its text, and the error printed both the same way
R1: review items were neither stored nor shown again before publish or enable, while the code and docs said a person confirms them first
minor: governed raw API calls counted as bounded (S4); recipient props came from adapter target lists and missed Discord's channel and attendee_email (S5)
the trigger was left out of sources and forbidden pieces (S6); 'reads from' was verified for a step that only sends (S7)
a cadence such as 'weekly' could only be stated as an exact cron (R2)
the abstention wording conflicted with F-08 (#755), and a merge could silently drop its ingredient checks (R3)
contract: null failed the compose (E1); the report was the last key of a capped result (E2)
test gaps, a mislabeled test, create tested only with an invalid contract, and the global time zone reset to null (T1)
the report and the stated contract shared one name (N1); the verified trigger line stated the time zone as if the graph proved it (N2)
suggestions_taken: one rule for open steps, with every universal claim withheld when one is present
recipients read from each step's inputs
a destination the job does not constrain is not checked
